title: Pronouns
intro:
• Genitive and dative singular: most pronouns have -īus in the genitive and -ī in the dative, for all three genders (illīus, illī; ipsīus, ipsī). Is, quī and hic do the same with their own spellings: eius, eī; cuius, cui; huius, huic.
  • Is, ea, id is the everyday 3rd-person pronoun (he, she, it). Its genitive (eius, eōrum, eārum) means his, her, its, their when it is not the subject's own; for the subject's own, Latin uses suus.
  • Quī, quae, quod takes its gender and number from the word it refers to, and its case from its own clause.
  • Suī has no nominative: it always points back to the subject of its own clause.
  • Ūnus nauta (ūnus, ūllus, nūllus, sōlus, neuter, alius, uter, tōtus, alter): ordinary -us, -a, -um adjectives except for the genitive -īus and dative -ī singular.
